q: What is the nearest airport to Bihać?
a: The nearest airports to Bihać are Zadar and Zagreb, about 150 to 165 km by road, or just over two hours' drive. In Bosnia and Herzegovina the closest is Banja Luka airport, with Rijeka and Sarajevo a little further away. Bihać has its own airfield at Golubić, but it has no scheduled passenger flights.

q: How far is Zagreb Airport from Bihać?
a: It is about 165 km from Zagreb Franjo Tuđman Airport to Bihać, roughly two and a half hours' drive without border queues. You take the motorway to Karlovac, then the main road via Slunj and Plitvice Lakes to the Izačić border crossing. In summer and at weekends, allow extra time for the border.

q: How far is Zadar Airport from Bihać?
a: Zadar Airport is about 150 km from Bihać, or just over two hours' drive. The usual route is north on the A1 motorway, then via Korenica and Plitvice Lakes to the Izačić border crossing. Zadar is a good option when there are cheap flights, especially in summer.

q: How far is Banja Luka Airport from Bihać?
a: Banja Luka is about 160 km from Bihać, and the airport, which lies north of the city, is a little further, so allow roughly two and a half to three hours' drive. The route goes via Prijedor, Novi Grad and Bosanska Krupa. The advantage is that you do not cross an international border.

q: How far is Sarajevo Airport from Bihać?
a: Sarajevo is about 290 to 310 km from Bihać, depending on the route, which is roughly five hours' drive. The road goes through central Bosnia, via Travnik or Jajce and then Ključ and Bosanska Krupa, so it is slower than a motorway. For visitors coming only to Bihać, Zagreb and Zadar are usually more convenient airports.

q: How long is the drive from Zagreb to Bihać?
a: Zagreb is about 160 km from Bihać, or two and a half hours' drive without border queues. You take the A1 motorway to Karlovac, then the D1 main road via Slunj to Plitvice and the Izačić border crossing. On the way you can stop at Rastoke in Slunj or at Plitvice Lakes.

q: What is the best route from Zagreb to Bihać?
a: The most common route is the motorway from Zagreb to Karlovac, then the D1 main road via Slunj to Plitvice Lakes, and on at Ličko Petrovo Selo to the Izačić border crossing. From Izačić it is about ten more kilometres to the centre of Bihać. The road is paved and well signposted all the way.

q: How far is Split from Bihać?
a: The drive from Split to Bihać takes around four hours, depending on the route and queues at the border. The simplest option is north on the A1 motorway, then through Lika and past Plitvice Lakes to the Izačić crossing. Check the route on your navigation before setting off, as journey times vary a lot depending on which roads you take.

q: How far is Vienna from Bihać?
a: Vienna is about 500 km from Bihać, roughly six hours' drive without long breaks or border queues. The route follows the motorway via Graz and Maribor to Zagreb, then via Karlovac and Slunj to the Izačić border. You need a road vignette for Austria and Slovenia, and you pay tolls on Croatian motorways.

q: How far is Ljubljana from Bihać?
a: Ljubljana is about 300 km from Bihać, roughly three and a half to four hours' drive. You take the motorway to Zagreb and then continue as from Zagreb, via Karlovac and Slunj to the Izačić border. Slovenian motorways require an e-vignette, while in Croatia tolls are paid per section.

q: How far is Munich from Bihać?
a: Munich is about 700 km from Bihać, roughly seven to eight hours' drive without long breaks. The usual route goes via Salzburg, the Karawanks Tunnel, Ljubljana and Zagreb, then via Karlovac to Bihać. You need a vignette for Austria and Slovenia, and there is a separate toll for the Karawanks Tunnel.

q: How do you get to Bihać from Germany?
a: From Germany most people drive to Bihać through Austria, Slovenia and Croatia, via Zagreb and Karlovac to the Izačić border. From southern Germany the drive takes seven hours or more, from the north about twice that. There are also bus services from German cities to Bihać; check timetables with the operators.

q: Is there a bus from Zagreb to Bihać?
a: Yes, there is a bus service between Zagreb and Bihać, but departures are few, usually one a day, and the journey takes a little over three hours. Check tickets and exact departure times at Zagreb Bus Station or with the operator before you travel. In summer and at weekends it is best to buy your ticket in advance.

q: Is there a bus from Germany or Austria to Bihać?
a: Yes, Bihać has bus connections with several cities in Germany, Austria and Slovenia, run by local and international operators. The journey from Munich takes about 11 to 12 hours. Timetables change with the season, so check with the operator or on bus ticket websites.

q: Is there a bus from Sarajevo to Bihać?
a: Yes, there are direct buses between Sarajevo and Bihać, and the journey takes about six to seven hours. Buses stop in several towns along the way, such as Travnik, Ključ or Bosanska Krupa, depending on the service. Check departures at Sarajevo bus station or with the operator.

q: Can you get to Bihać by train?
a: Regular passenger trains to Bihać are not currently a practical way to arrive, so most visitors come by car or bus. In summer 2026, Federation of BiH Railways (Željeznice FBiH) ran a weekend tourist train along the Una between Bihać and Bosanska Otoka. Check the current timetable on the Željeznice FBiH website.

q: How far is Karlovac from Bihać?
a: Karlovac is about 100 km from Bihać, roughly an hour and a half to two hours' drive without border queues. You take the D1 main road via Slunj and Rakovica to Plitvice Lakes, then at Ličko Petrovo Selo to the Izačić border crossing. There are no tolls on this stretch.

q: Where is the bus station in Bihać?
a: Bihać bus station is in town, not far from the centre, so most apartments in the centre can be reached on foot or by a short taxi ride. From the houses in Lohovo, Pritoka or Grmuša you will need a taxi or a lift from your host. If you are arriving by bus, mention it in your enquiry and we will tell you how to get to the property; we speak English and German.

q: Are there taxis in Bihać?
a: Yes, there are taxi companies in Bihać, and journeys within town are usually short and inexpensive. You can find taxis at the bus station and in the centre, or call one by phone. For longer trips, for example to Grmuša or Lohovo, agree the fare before you set off.

q: Is there an airport transfer from Zagreb to Bihać?
a: Yes, private transfers from Zagreb Airport to Bihać can be booked, and the journey takes about two and a half hours plus any border wait. A transfer is practical for families and groups, as the price is per vehicle. If you need transport to our property, mention it in your enquiry at apartmanibihac.com or on WhatsApp +387 61 591 320.

q: Do I need a car in Bihać?
a: If you stay in the centre of Bihać, you do not need a car for the town itself, as everything is within walking distance. For the houses on the Una in Lohovo and Grmuša, and for trips to Štrbački Buk and Plitvice, a car is very useful. Guests without a car usually choose apartments in the centre, such as Apartman Centar or Apartman City Centar.

q: Can you hire a car in Bihać?
a: There are a few local car hire firms in Bihać, but the choice is smaller than in Zagreb or Zadar. If you are flying in, it is easiest to hire a car at the airport. Check with the rental company whether the contract allows you to enter Bosnia and Herzegovina, as some Croatian rentals charge extra for this or require special permission.

q: Can I take a hire car from Croatia into Bosnia and Herzegovina?
a: Usually yes, but only if the rental agreement allows it, so state clearly when booking that you are going to Bosnia and Herzegovina. Some companies charge an extra fee or require a special document for the border. At the border you must have the vehicle registration document and the rental agreement.

q: Is there parking in Bihać?
a: Yes, Bihać has public car parks, and in the centre parking is mostly paid by zone, as shown on the signs. Most of our properties have their own parking, and the description of each property on apartmanibihac.com says whether it does. That way you can leave the car at your accommodation and explore the town on foot.

q: Is parking free at the accommodation?
a: At most of our properties parking is next to the building and included in the price, for example at Apartman Hari, Apartman M. Mahala, Feel Luxury and LUX Apartments. The houses on the Una in Lohovo, Pritoka and Grmuša have parking in the garden or next to the house. If you are coming with a van or several cars, mention it in your enquiry.

q: Are there tolls between Zagreb and Bihać?
a: On the Croatian side you only pay a toll for the motorway from Zagreb to Karlovac, if you use it; the stretch from Karlovac via Slunj to the border is a free main road. In Bosnia and Herzegovina there is no motorway and no toll on the way to Bihać. Check toll amounts on the Croatian Motorways (Hrvatske autoceste) website.

q: How do you pay motorway tolls in Croatia?
a: On Croatian motorways tolls are currently still mostly paid at toll booths, in cash, by card or with an ENC electronic device. Croatia is preparing to switch to barrier-free tolling with number-plate recognition, so the rules are changing. Before you travel, check the current payment method on the official Croatian Motorways website.

q: Do you need a vignette for Bosnia and Herzegovina?
a: No, Bosnia and Herzegovina has no vignette system, and tolls are only charged on motorways, of which there are none on the way to Bihać. You do need a vignette if you drive through Slovenia or Austria. In Croatia you pay tolls per motorway section. Buy the Slovenian e-vignette and Austrian vignette in advance from the official websites.

q: What are the roads like to Bihać?
a: The roads to Bihać are paved and mostly in good condition, but from Karlovac onwards you drive on main roads with one lane in each direction. The stretch via Slunj and Plitvice can be busy in summer with tourists and lorries. The last part of the road to Štrbački Buk is gravel, so drive slowly.

q: Do you need winter tyres in Bosnia and Herzegovina?
a: Yes, winter equipment is compulsory in Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1 November to 1 April, regardless of the weather. This means winter tyres on all wheels, or summer tyres with at least 4 mm of tread plus snow chains in the car. In Croatia the winter period on designated roads runs from 15 November to 15 April. In winter, check road conditions with BIHAMK and the Croatian Auto Club (HAK) before setting off.

q: How long is the drive from Bihać to Plitvice Lakes?
a: It is about 35 km from Bihać to the entrance of Plitvice Lakes National Park, or 35 to 40 minutes' drive without border queues. You go via the Izačić border crossing and Ličko Petrovo Selo. In summer set off early, as queues build up at the border and in the park's car parks.

q: How long is the border wait on the way to Bihać?
a: At the Izačić crossing the wait is usually anything from a few minutes to half an hour, but in summer, on public holidays and at weekends it can be over an hour. The busiest times are Saturdays and Sundays and the start and end of school holidays. Check the border situation before setting off on the motoring clubs' or border police websites.

q: Are there petrol stations on the way to Bihać?
a: Yes, there are petrol stations along the motorway to Karlovac, in Slunj and around Plitvice, and several at the entrances to Bihać. Fuel in Bosnia and Herzegovina is usually a little cheaper than in Croatia, so many drivers fill up after the border. In Bosnia and Herzegovina you pay in convertible marks or by card.

q: Which border crossing is quickest for Bihać?
a: The quickest and most used route from Croatia is the Ličko Petrovo Selo – Izačić crossing, about ten kilometres from the centre of Bihać. Coming from the south via Donji Lapac, you can also enter at Užljebić, and from the north at Maljevac towards Velika Kladuša. Before you travel, check which crossings are open to international traffic.

q: How do I get to Grmuša from Bihać?
a: Grmuša is about 20 km north-east of Bihać, along the Una towards Bosanska Krupa. The drive takes about twenty minutes. If you are rafting with Una Olympic Rafting or staying in one of our houses in Grmuša, you will receive exact directions once your booking is confirmed.

q: How do I get to Lohovo from Bihać?
a: Lohovo is about 10 km south of Bihać, along the Una towards Ripač and Una National Park. The drive takes around fifteen minutes. Our riverside houses are here, including Vila Enio with its swimming pool, and you will receive the exact address and directions once your booking is confirmed.

q: How do I get to Pritoka?
a: Pritoka is on the edge of Bihać by the Una, a few minutes' drive from the town centre. It is easy to reach by car or taxi, and from Pritoka you can also take a longer walk into the centre. One of our properties here is Vikendica Rekić, a house with access to the Una for up to eight people.

q: Where to stop on the way from Zagreb to Bihać?
a: The best-known stops on the way from Zagreb to Bihać are Rastoke in Slunj, an old village with the Slunjčica waterfalls, and Plitvice Lakes National Park. Both are on the main road, so you do not need to leave your route. Visiting Plitvice takes several hours, so many people save it for a separate day trip from Bihać.

q: How far is Rijeka from Bihać?
a: Rijeka is about 200 km from Bihać, and the drive takes around three hours. You can take the motorway towards Zagreb as far as Karlovac and then go via Slunj, or take the A6 and A1 motorways south to Otočac and then go via Plitvice. Both routes end at the Izačić border crossing.

q: Can you get to Bihać by motorbike or bicycle?
a: Yes, the roads to Bihać and the Una valley are popular with motorcyclists and cyclists, especially the route via Plitvice and along the river towards Una National Park. Main roads are busy in summer, so cyclists are safer on quieter side roads. Apartman M. Mahala (Midžić Mahala) has space for bicycles; for other properties, just ask when you enquire.
